recipes.name: Chicken, Stuffing and Green Bean Casserole
ingredients_raw: 2 cups cooked, cubed chicken breast meat
1 (10.75 ounce) can condensed cream of chicken soup
1 (12 ounce) package unseasoned dry bread stuffing mix

steps.text: Combine chicken, soup, beans, salt, and pepper in a medium bowl; mix well and set aside.
Prepare stuffing according to package directions. Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).
Spoon chicken mixture into a 9x13 inch baking dish; top with prepared stuffing and sprinkle with cheese.
Bake, covered, for 25 minutes; remove cover and bake until cheese is golden brown and melted on top, about 5 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Chicken, Stuffing and Green Bean Casserole
raw_recipe.description: A creamy chicken and green bean casserole topped with stuffing mix and Cheddar cheese, baked into a simple and delicious dinner.

review.reviewBody: This is a good family meal recipe. ---I varied the recipe a bit. I used uncooked chicken breasts and let them cook with the casserole (350 for an hour)and added some cheese whiz (because I did not have a lot of cheddar cheese on hand). Also used frozen green beans and cream of mushroom soup.-- Thanks.

I made this dish for Thanksgiving and it was absolutely delicious! Reading other reviews, I did make some changes to the recipe. I used cream of mushroom and added a small can of sliced mushrooms (cause I love mushrooms). I also added 1/2 cup 1% low fat milk and cooked the chicken with a couple chopped up cloves of garlic. I did not add any extra salt, but did pepper it a little, used "no salt added" green beans and Stovetops Chicken stuffing. Only used about 1/2 cup of cheese (chedder & jack) to sprinkle on then topped it off with about 1 1/2 cup of french fried onions. Very easy recipe and very very good! My boyfriend is now requesting I make it all the time!

I thought this was excellent. I used leftover chicken breasts cubed rather then can chicken. I also wanted to make a double batch so I used 1 can of cream of chicken soup and 1 cheddar cheese soup. I then cut down on the amount of cheese on the top to just a sprinkling. I added some chopped onion and a little garlic for extra flavor. I also used flavored stuffing because that's what I had on hand. I have 3 super picky eaters and they loved it. As someone else mentioned the leftovers almost tasted better then it did the first time.

The kids & I enjoyed this simple meal, hubbys flying home from a business trip as I type so he didn't get to vote (nor does he get any casserole because there was none left). I used a 6 oz. box of brownberry stuffing & that was plenty. Next time I will go for the sage, or onion & garlic flavored stuffing. Thanks so much Cathy!

Made this for a potluck and got requests for the recipe--great family fare! I'm not a fan of canned green beans, so I used a 20-oz bag of frozen green beans (microwaved 5 minutes and drained). As others suggested, I opted for mushroom soup instead of chicken soup, added 1/2 c. milk, and eliminated the salt. For the stuffing, I used a 12-oz. box of Mrs. Cubbison's Cornbread Stuffin', which I already had on hand. Yummy!

This looked pretty darn good, but the amount of ingredients seemed way too light for a 13x9 pan, so I made some changes. Go ahead, bash me. First, I used a rotisserie chicken instead of cooked breasts. Second, I used 1 can of cream of chicken along with an 8oz container of sour cream. Third, I had leftover frozen green beans, white corn, and peas from vegetable soup that I boiled up with no salt. I used Stove Top cornbread stuffing for the topping, with no cheese. I did prepare this earlier in the day and refrigerated it, so my bake time was about 30 minutes civered, then about 15 minutes uncovered, and 10 minutes max under the broiler. It was about a foot down from the broiler. This came out tasting just awesome! I'm really glad I didn't use cheese. I had this with mashed potatoes boiled in heavy cream, the only way to make mashed potatoes, trust me on that! I will definitely be making this meal again in the future!!

I love this recipe and make it often! If you only have uncooked chicken breasts, just cut it in strips and lay it in the bottom of a casserole dish-top with green beans and cream soup, (you can also use a white sauce if you don't have soup); then top with your stuffing mix. Cook at 350 about 45 minutes covered- then 15 minutes more uncovered. Personally, no cheese is needed for this recipe. I top with just a little of the white sauce.
Great dish. I used the Durkee French fried onions on top of stuffing and added some corn as well. Turned out great. My boyfriend loved it!!!!!!

I made a few changes only because I know what my family likes. I sautéed onions and celery and added it to the stuffing. I used a 6 oz package of Stove Top and that was plenty. I added a can of mushrooms and omitted the cheese. After mixing the chicken mixture I didn’t think there was enough for a 9 x 13 dish so I baked it in an 8 x 8 dish and it worked out perfectly. Thanks for the recipe.
This was absolutely wonderful! Definantly comfort food. I used sage stuffing instead of plain and its also great without the chicken (I've made it both ways).

Mmmm I think this was very good and very easy to make. I liked eating the leftovers the next day. My daughter said she didn't like it but she did finish her whole plate. My husband said it was good and he did have 2nds. I am going to make this again soon because I want more. I used low sodium soup and rinsed the green beans and did not add extra salt, so it wasn't at all too salty. I mixed in half a can of milk (so it was more creamy and not as thick) and a little cheddar cheese in the soup mixture as well as adding the full cup of cheese on top, I thought it was good with the cheese.

This was very good. I seasoned two chicken breasts with garlic granules and black pepper, then dipped both sides in melted butter and coated with bread crumbs. Baked the chicken uncovered for 30 minutes at 350. Cooled it a bit and cut in bite size pieces. I used fresh green beans from a neighbor, which I had boiled the day before. Because I used more beans and chicken than the recipe called for, I used 1 1/2 cans cream of chicken soup. I used a box of unseaoned cornbread stuffing mix and added thyme and sage to it. My family loved it. I think I would have given it five stars if I had added celery to the stuffing, and mushrooms.

I boiled a whole chicken with proper seasoning... celery and onions, used fresh green beans steamed... homemade stuffing like my grandma made, and homemade garlic mashed potatoes and gravy on the side...omg... freaking delicious! Yes I could have done rotisserie chicken and stove top to make it way quicker, but I had the time to make everything from scratch!
My family scarfed it up. Delicious and easy.

This was pretty good. I substituted leftover turkey and cream of mushroom soup, added a small can of sliced mushrooms and some milk. I also used turkey stove top stuffing, made according to the instructions, before topping the casserole. I used an 11” by 7” casserole dish and it was perfect.
Easy to make! Just seasoned with garlic powder and ground pepper and replaced the chicken soup for mushroom
I made added a cup of water, lawrys seasoning salt, a sprinkling of grated Parmesan and cheddar cheese. (Less than the recipe recommended). It was delicious. I will definitely make again sometime.

I have made this following the directions above, and it was yummy. I was in a hurry today, and just put everything in the bowl and added enough chicken broth to reach the right consistency. I actually prefer it just all mixed together! Either way, this is a simple and tasty recipe that will be in my "regular rotation"!
Very tasty! Used chopped leftover rotisserie chicken and Italian green beans added sour cream. Next time I may add mixed veggies.
Same as my mom’s “chicken stuff”. Loved it then and love it now.
